title: Confidential Information and Unauthorized Disclosure
definition: A secrecy violation occurs when a person discloses, shares, forwards, provides access to, discusses, or improperly handles confidential, restricted, proprietary, sensitive, or otherwise protected company information without appropriate authorization. The model must evaluate the meaning and context of the communication and must not classify an email as a secrecy violation merely because it mentions confidential information, documents, agreements, customers, projects, or confidentiality.
violations: Disclosing confidential or restricted company information to a person who is not authorized to receive it

Sharing confidential documents, files, information, customer information, business details, financial information, technical information, or internal company information with an unauthorized recipient
Forwarding or providing access to protected company information without authorization
Improperly handling confidential information in a way that exposes it to unauthorized individuals
Requesting or encouraging another person to disclose protected company information without authorization
Sending or discussing protected information through an unauthorized person, account, system, or communication channel
Providing confidential information to an external party without appropriate authorization
Sharing restricted information with a colleague who does not have a legitimate need or authorization to receive it
Instructing another person to bypass confidentiality controls in order to obtain or share protected information
Attempting to conceal an unauthorized disclosure of protected information
Using protected company information for an unauthorized personal or external purpose
exceptions: Legitimate instructions to keep information confidential
Instructions that prevent disclosure of information until an agreement, contract, or authorization is formally completed
Disclosure that is explicitly authorized by the appropriate company authority
Sharing information with a recipient who is explicitly authorized to receive it
Routine business communication that does not disclose protected or restricted information
Mentioning confidentiality, agreements, contracts, projects, customers, documents, or protected information without actually disclosing the protected contents
Discussing the importance of protecting confidential information without requesting or performing an unauthorized disclosure
Requesting authorization before sharing protected information
Reporting a suspected unauthorized disclosure to an appropriate authority
examples: Sending a confidential company document to an unauthorized external recipient
Forwarding restricted business information to someone who is not authorized to receive it
Providing an unauthorized person with access to confidential company files
Sending customer information to a personal email account without authorization
Asking a colleague to send confidential project information to an external contact
Telling a recipient not to disclose an agreement until it has been formally signed is not itself an unauthorized disclosure
Discussing the need to keep an agreement confidential without revealing its protected contents is not a secrecy violation
Mentioning a confidential project without revealing confidential information is not automatically a secrecy violation

title: Improper Payments, Gifts, and Benefits
definition: A market bribery violation occurs when a person offers, promises, gives, requests, accepts, or arranges an improper payment, gift, benefit, favor, service, hospitality, or other advantage with the purpose or expectation of improperly influencing a business, commercial, regulatory, or market-related decision. The model must evaluate intent, context, and the connection between the benefit and the decision rather than flagging ordinary gifts, meals, drinks, entertainment, or business expenses automatically.
violations: Offering money or another improper benefit in exchange for favorable business treatment
Requesting or accepting an improper payment or benefit to influence a business decision
Offering a gift, favor, service, meal, entertainment, drink, or advantage with the intention of improperly influencing a decision
Agreeing to provide an improper benefit in return for preferential treatment
Using an intermediary or third party to provide an improper payment or benefit intended to influence a business decision
Discussing or arranging an improper payment or benefit for the purpose of obtaining an unfair business advantage
Offering personal benefits to a decision-maker in exchange for approval, a contract, business opportunity, regulatory treatment, or preferential treatment
Requesting a personal payment, gift, favor, or benefit in exchange for performing or approving a business activity
Arranging gifts, payments, entertainment, or benefits specifically to influence a business, commercial, regulatory, or market-related decision
Attempting to hide or disguise an improper payment or benefit intended to influence a decision
exceptions: Legitimate business expenses that are permitted under applicable company policy
Ordinary business activities that do not involve an attempt to improperly influence a decision
Benefits that are explicitly permitted and appropriately authorized under company policy
Routine discussion of gifts, meals, drinks, entertainment, expenses, or business benefits without an improper purpose
Discussing an approved business expense without requesting or offering an improper advantage
Legitimate business hospitality that is permitted by company policy and does not influence a decision
Rejecting, reporting, or discussing concerns about a potentially improper payment or benefit
A social activity or business meal without evidence of an attempt to influence a decision
examples: Offering money to a business partner in exchange for awarding a contract
Offering an inappropriate gift to influence a customer's purchasing decision
Requesting a personal payment in exchange for approving a business transaction
Arranging for another person to provide a benefit in exchange for preferential treatment
Offering expensive entertainment specifically to obtain favorable business treatment
Offering a gift before a decision-maker approves a contract in order to influence the decision
Discussing an ordinary authorized business meal without attempting to influence a business decision is not bribery
Mentioning drinks or gifts without connecting them to improper influence is not automatically bribery

title: Artificial or Misleading Market Activity
definition: A market manipulation violation occurs when a person intentionally attempts to artificially influence the price, supply, demand, trading activity, or market perception of a financial instrument through deceptive, misleading, coordinated, or artificial actions. The model must distinguish legitimate market discussion, analysis, trading, and investment activity from communications that actually instruct, encourage, arrange, or promote artificial or deceptive market activity.
violations: Intentionally creating artificial buying or selling activity to influence a market price
Coordinating transactions for the purpose of artificially increasing or decreasing a financial instrument's price
Creating false or misleading market activity to influence other market participants
Spreading false or misleading information with the intention of influencing trading activity or market prices
Using deceptive transactions or trading strategies to create a false impression of market demand or supply
Encouraging another person to participate in activity intended to artificially influence market conditions
Planning or arranging transactions specifically to create an artificial market price
Coordinating with others to create artificial demand, supply, trading volume, or market activity
Instructing another person to create misleading market activity
Intentionally distributing false information to influence another person's trading decision
Attempting to conceal an artificial or deceptive trading strategy
Creating a false appearance of market interest, demand, supply, liquidity, or trading activity
exceptions: Legitimate market analysis that does not involve deceptive or artificial activity
Ordinary trading or investment decisions made for legitimate business or investment purposes
Accurate communication of publicly available market information without an intention to mislead
Legitimate discussion of market conditions without instructions to manipulate market activity
General discussion of prices, markets, securities, trading, or investment strategies without evidence of manipulation
Legitimate research or analysis that does not instruct or encourage artificial market activity
Good-faith discussion of possible market scenarios without an instruction or intention to manipulate the market
Reporting or discussing suspected market manipulation for legitimate compliance purposes
examples: Coordinating transactions specifically to artificially increase the price of a security
Creating misleading trading activity to make market demand appear higher than it actually is
Sharing intentionally false information to influence another person's trading decision
Planning transactions specifically to create an artificial market price
Asking others to create buying activity so that a security appears more popular than it really is
Coordinating trades specifically to make trading volume appear artificially high
Discussing normal market conditions without instructions to create artificial activity is not market manipulation
Discussing legitimate market analysis without an intention to mislead is not market manipulation

title: Employee Ethical Conduct
definition: An employee ethics violation occurs when an employee engages in dishonest, deceptive, inappropriate, unprofessional, improper, or unethical conduct that conflicts with company standards, employee responsibilities, or expected professional behavior. The model must evaluate the complete meaning and context of the communication rather than relying on individual keywords. Ordinary, harmless, casual, informal, incomplete, or unclear communication is not automatically an ethics violation.
violations: Knowingly providing false or misleading information for an improper purpose
Using an employee's position, authority, access, or influence for an improper personal benefit
Engaging in dishonest or deceptive conduct related to company business
Intentionally concealing relevant information for the purpose of obtaining an improper benefit
Using company resources, information, systems, or authority for an unauthorized personal purpose
Engaging in conduct that creates an undisclosed or improperly managed conflict of interest
Using an employee's position or company relationship to obtain improper preferential treatment
Engaging in inappropriate, unprofessional, disrespectful, or improper behavior in a work-related context
Making inappropriate requests, suggestions, arrangements, or instructions that conflict with expected employee conduct
Encouraging, arranging, or participating in inappropriate conduct involving employees or business contacts
Engaging in inappropriate behavior at or in connection with company-related activities, meetings, events, or business interactions
Using company communication channels or business relationships for an improper personal purpose
Attempting to conceal improper employee conduct from the company or relevant authority
Knowingly violating expected professional standards for the purpose of obtaining a personal or improper advantage
Requesting or encouraging another employee to participate in improper or unethical conduct
exceptions: Ordinary mistakes that do not involve intentional dishonesty or improper conduct
Good-faith business decisions made within the employee's responsibilities
Legitimate use of company resources for authorized business purposes
Routine professional communication that does not demonstrate unethical or inappropriate behavior
Casual, informal, incomplete, or unclear communication that does not contain sufficient evidence of improper conduct
Clearly personal communication that does not involve company business, company resources, employee responsibilities, or improper conduct
Legitimate employee social activities that are authorized and do not involve inappropriate behavior
Ordinary discussion of food, drinks, entertainment, meetings, social activities, or personal matters without evidence of unethical or improper conduct
Good-faith reporting of inappropriate or unethical behavior
Legitimate requests for clarification, assistance, or guidance regarding employee responsibilities
examples: Knowingly providing false information to obtain an improper personal benefit
Using an employee's position to obtain preferential treatment for a personal matter
Concealing a relevant conflict of interest while making a related business decision
Using company information for an unauthorized personal purpose
Using company resources for an unauthorized personal activity
Making an inappropriate request to another employee for a personal benefit
Arranging inappropriate conduct involving employees during a work-related activity
Engaging in unprofessional or improper behavior during a company-related event
Attempting to hide improper employee conduct from management or compliance
A casual message mentioning drinks, food, entertainment, or social activities without evidence of improper conduct is not automatically an employee ethics violation
A message containing an actual inappropriate request, arrangement, or behavior must be evaluated based on the surrounding context rather than the presence of a single keyword

title: Complaint Handling and Reporting
definition: A complaints-related violation occurs when a legitimate complaint or concern involving employee conduct, business practices, or company processes is improperly ignored, suppressed, mishandled, discouraged, concealed, or intentionally prevented from reaching the appropriate reporting or review process. The model must distinguish between a person reporting or discussing a complaint and a person attempting to suppress, ignore, or improperly handle it.
violations: Intentionally preventing a legitimate complaint from being reported through the appropriate process
Ignoring a complaint that requires investigation or appropriate handling
Suppressing or concealing a legitimate complaint or concern
Improperly handling a formal complaint in a way that prevents appropriate review
Discouraging a person from reporting a legitimate concern through an approved reporting process
Retaliating against or improperly treating a person because they raised a legitimate complaint
Instructing another person not to report a legitimate concern
Attempting to hide a complaint or concern from compliance, management, HR, or another appropriate authority
Destroying, withholding, or manipulating information to prevent a legitimate complaint from being investigated
Attempting to resolve or close a legitimate complaint outside the required process specifically to prevent review
Threatening or pressuring a person to withdraw a legitimate complaint
exceptions: A person simply reporting a legitimate concern or complaint
Routine communication about a complaint that does not suppress, ignore, or improperly handle the complaint
Resolving a complaint through an authorized company process
Requesting additional information needed to properly investigate a complaint
Discussing the existence or status of a complaint without attempting to suppress or prevent appropriate reporting
Providing legitimate assistance or guidance to someone who wants to report a concern
Forwarding a complaint to the appropriate team for investigation
Requesting clarification about a complaint in good faith
Discussing a complaint without attempting to influence whether it is reported or investigated
examples: Telling an employee not to report a legitimate workplace concern
Ignoring a formal complaint that requires investigation
Attempting to prevent a complaint from reaching the appropriate compliance team
Suppressing a legitimate complaint to avoid an investigation
Threatening an employee because they submitted a complaint
Asking someone to withdraw a complaint so that the company does not investigate it
Reporting a legitimate complaint through an approved process is not a complaints violation
Asking for additional information needed to investigate a complaint is not a violation

title: Unauthorized Communication Channels
definition: A change in communication violation occurs when business-related communication is moved, continued, redirected, or intentionally arranged through a personal or external communication channel that is not approved for company business. The model must determine whether the communication is actually business-related and whether the external channel is unauthorized. Mentioning an external service or using it for clearly personal communication is not automatically a violation.
violations: Moving a business discussion from an approved company channel to a personal or external communication channel
Asking another person to continue business-related communication through a personal or external messaging service
Using a personal or external communication service to continue discussions concerning company business, agreements, transactions, or other work-related matters
Redirecting business communication to an external channel specifically to avoid or bypass an approved company communication system
Continuing a business discussion through an external communication method when the communication concerns company work or a business agreement
Requesting a colleague or business contact to use a personal account for company-related communication
Moving confidential, transactional, contractual, or work-related discussions to an unauthorized external channel
Using a personal phone, email, messaging application, or other external service to conduct company business when the channel is not approved
Attempting to avoid company monitoring, retention, approval, or compliance controls by moving business communication to an external channel
Arranging future business communication through an unauthorized external channel
exceptions: The external communication channel is explicitly approved for the relevant business activity
The communication is clearly personal and unrelated to company business
The external channel is being used for a legitimate purpose specifically authorized by the company
Mentioning WhatsApp, personal email, phone, or another external service without requesting or directing business communication to that service
Personal communication that has no connection to company business, agreements, transactions, or work-related matters
Discussing an external communication channel without actually moving or requesting movement of business communication
Using an approved external communication service for an authorized business purpose
Discussing personal social activities with a colleague without moving business communication to an unauthorized channel
examples: Asking a business contact to continue a company discussion through a personal messaging service
Moving a discussion about a business agreement to an external messaging application
Asking someone to continue company-related communication through a personal account
Inviting a business contact to continue work-related communication outside the approved company communication system
Asking a colleague to send company documents to a personal email address
Moving a business transaction discussion to a personal messaging application to avoid company monitoring
Mentioning WhatsApp in an unrelated personal conversation is not a change-in-communication violation
Discussing plans to meet socially without moving business communication to an external channel is not a violation
